assumptions: Source assumption: CBR and CDR are same-period crude rates on the same per-1000 base and reference population (World Bank RNI sentence; Eurostat crude-rates paragraph).
Application profile: RNI equals the rate of population change in the absence of migration (World Bank statistical concepts); with migration present it is one component, not total growth.
Source assumption: inputs are period accounting rates, not forecasts; no exponential or projection machinery is used.

gaps: New meaning natural_increase_rate is absent from the supplied runtime vocabulary; extension required.
Per-1000 convention is inherited from the CBR/CDR inputs with no added scaling literal; output unit 1 matches inputs.

models.inverse_notes: Forward solves RNI from CBR and CDR. Inverses: CBR = RNI + CDR needs RNI and CDR; CDR = CBR - RNI needs CBR and RNI. No division, so no singularities; nonnegativity guards on CBR/CDR persist (e.g. RNI = 9 with CDR = 9.5 gives CBR = 18.5, matching reference rni-ordinary; RNI = -2 with CBR = 12 gives CDR = 14). Substitution checks pass. Signed RNI is meaningful (natural decrease); algebraic inversion implies no causality.
limitations: Covers natural change only: in the presence of migration, RNI is not the total growth rate (World Bank: equal to change in the absence of migration).
Inherits crude-rate limits: no age-structure adjustment, so cross-population comparison needs care (World Bank/Hageman).
Rate inputs are not defaults: no fixed CBR/CDR value is reused as a default.

models.inverse_notes: Forward solves net migration M from I and E. Inverses: I = M + E needs M and E; E = I - M needs I and M. No division, so no singularities; nonnegativity guards on I/E persist (e.g. M = 2000 with E = 3000 gives I = 5000, matching reference migration-inflow; M = -3000 with I = 1000 gives E = 4000). Signed M is meaningful (net outflow); algebraic inversion implies no causality.
limitations: Measured flows only: Eurostat net-migration-plus-adjustment can bundle coverage error with I - E, and Hageman notes emigration must often be inferred; residuals are outside this identity.
Explains nothing by itself: separating accounting from causal or forecast claims about why migration took the supplied values.
Counts are not defaults: no fixed migration value is reused as a default input.

references.provenance: Independent elementary arithmetic check with synthetic flows.

references.method: Direct subtraction with signed outcome: 1000 - 4000 = -3000 net outflow (supported by net-migration sign convention).
references.provenance: Independent elementary arithmetic check demonstrating the signed scope.

relationship.original_equation: M = I − E (net migration equals immigration/inflows minus emigration/outflows in the period)
relationship.translation_notes: I maps immigrants/inflows and E maps emigrants/outflows for the same area, residency and period. No scaling literal and no unit conversion: canonical unit is person (scale 1) for every flow, each event counting one usually-resident person. Dimensional check: population − population = population. Signed output is deliberate (negative = net outflow). This two-input count is the migration arm of the b01 balance P1 = P0 + B - D + M.
